title: Core/shell Printing Scaffolds For Tissue Engineering Of Tubular Structures
protocol: Dissolve ALG and CMC powders in ultra-pure water to obtain a total 3 wt% ALG and 3 wt% CMC solution.
Add 1.5 wt% cellulose nanofibers to the ALG-CMC mixture for additional mechanical reinforcement.
Agitate the hydrogel suspension until homogeneous using an overhead mixer.
Prepare 10 mL of 100 mM calcium chloride (CaCl2) solution in ultra-pure water.
Prepare 10 mL of 5 wt.% CaCl2 solution in ultra-pure water.
Sterilize the bioprinter by spraying 70% ethanol thoroughly.
Expose the bioprinter to UV light for 1 hour.
Turn on the bioprinter and run the controlling software.
Perform the homing procedure by pressing the Home icon.
Import the generated scaffold g-code using the File | Import G-Code command.
Transfer the hydrogel to a sterile 5 mL syringe and place it in one of the extruder mounts of the 3D printer.
Connect the syringe via luer-lock and short tube to side luer input of the core/shell nozzle.
Transfer 100 mM CaCl2 cross-linking solution to a sterile 5 mL syringe with an attached G27 blunt-end needle.
Insert the syringe into the top needle holder of the core/shell nozzle so that the inner needle protrudes about 1 mm from the outer nozzle.
Manually adjust the alignment of the needles.
Insert a second syringe into the extrusion mount for hydrogel.
Extrude both the hydrogel and cross-linking solution separately to remove all air bubbles.
Adjust the distance between the nozzle and printing substrate using the Z and Up/Down arrows.
Set up on a flat, glass-printing substrate with good adhesion.
Ensure that the extrusion nozzle is not in contact with the substrate for uninterrupted flow of the hydrogel.
Press the Play button to start the printing process.
Print a skirt surrounding the scaffold before starting the actual scaffold printing.
Vary formulation composition and cross-linking solution composition for optimal hydrogel flow.
Adjust printing parameters such as speed, pressure, temperature, and nozzle-to-substrate distance.
Pour 5 wt.% CaCl2 secondary cross-linking solution over the entire scaffold after printing.
Incubate the scaffold in the cross-linking solution at room temperature for 1 minute.
Ensure the entire scaffold is submerged during incubation.
Manually cut excess skirt material with a scalpel.
Sterilize scaffolds under UV light for 30 minutes on one side.
Carefully flip the scaffold and sterilize the other side under UV light for 30 minutes.
Gently pull the scaffold sideways to detach it from the substrate.
If the scaffold adheres strongly, separate it by inserting a sharp edge between them.
Transfer the scaffold into colorless cell culture media (DMEM supplemented with 5 wt.% FBS, 100 U/mL penicillin and 1 mg/mL streptomycin).
Incubate the scaffolds at 37°C in an atmosphere containing 5 wt.% CO2 for at least 24 h.
Prepare advanced DMEM cell culture medium with phenol red, supplemented with 5 wt.% FBS and 2 mM L-glutamine.
Add 100 U/mL penicillin and 1 mg/mL streptomycin to the medium.
Initiate human umbilical vein endothelial cell (HUVEC) line in accordance with HUVEC culturing protocols.
Pipette 100 μL of cells suspended in cell culture media for staining.
Stain cells with 900 μL of 0.1 wt.% trypan blue solution.
Count and obtain the estimated number of cells in suspension using an automated cell counter or manual hemocytometer.
Prepare a live/dead assay solution of 4 mM Calcein-AM and 2 mM propidium iodide in sterile PBS immediately before conducting the assay.
Remove scaffolds from cell culture media and transfer them into a sufficiently large glass Petri dish.
Dispose of cell culture media from HUVECs in flasks.
Incubate cells with 0.25 wt.% trypsin (~2 mL) for 5 min at 37 °C.
Add ~3 mL of cell culture media to the trypsinized cells and transfer them to a centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge the cells at 200 x g for 5 min.
Dispose of the supernatant from the centrifuged cells.
Resuspend the cells in fresh cell culture media.
Count the cells as described previously.
Adjust the total cell concentration to 340,000 cells/mL.
Resuspend the cells in a sterile syringe with an attached blunt G27 needle.
Find an entry point and start carefully injecting cells into the scaffolds.
Submerge the scaffolds in cell culture media and incubate them at 37 °C in an atmosphere containing 5 wt.% CO₂ for up to 10 days.
Replenish the cell culture media according to experimental needs.
Rinse the scaffolds with PBS after incubation.
With a blunt-end needle, carefully inject the live/dead solution (4 mM calcein-AM and 2 mM propidium iodide in PBS) into the scaffolds.
Incubate the scaffolds in PBS for 30 min at 37 °C.
Rinse the scaffolds with PBS.
Carefully transfer the scaffolds to a glass slide.
Observe the dyed cells directly in the scaffolds under a fluorescence microscope.
